description: CHARIM (Caribbean Handbook on Risk Information Management) was a World Bank-funded project that produced national hazard maps and guidance for small eastern Caribbean states, and its handbook with country data is kept in the virtual library of the Caribbean Disaster Emergency Management Agency (CDEMA). The Saint Vincent and the Grenadines maps page read on 2026-09-28 offers PDF versions of a topographic map, a land cover map, a national flood hazard map from 2016 with its flood hazard assessment report, a landslide inventory map with its report and a landslide susceptibility map, each linked to a view on the CHARIM GeoNode; the country data section has matching pages for Grenada and Saint Lucia, and the handbook also covers Dominica and Belize. Coverage is national for each state. Access is free download; no licence is stated. Caveats: the maps date from the project years around 2016 and are not updated, the GeoNode links were not checked and may be offline, and PDFs are maps, not GIS layers. It supports hazard exposure of roads, buildings and critical facilities to floods and landslides. Related record: data-cdema-situation-reports complements it with event reports.
